newsitem.title: UK: UK shares seen mixed as options expiry looms.
newsitem.headline: UK shares seen mixed as options expiry looms.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index was expected to open mixed to lower on Friday as investors continue the profit-taking which sent UK shares lower the previous session.
A weaker performance in New York was also expected to take its toll though the Dow finished a modest 18 points lower on the day.

"Wall Street was slightly easier and we were selling off before the close yesterday so I expect we'll open a tad easier today," said one senior trader. "Yesterday we were in a downtrend and trends don't just stop after one day."
The FTSE 100 rose to within a whisker of the 5,000 barrier on Thursday before recoiling to end 15.2 points lower on the day at 4,949.0.

"With a slightly weaker finish on Wall Street, that will probably be enough for people to want to carry on from yesterday," said one equity salesman. "Friday is never a great day to start a new initiative."
But with July index options expiry between 1010-1030 BST, activity in the futures market is likely to set direction soon after the opening and traders predicted a volatile ride.
"We could actually jump 25-points either way as the options expiry gets closer," one derivatives specialist said.
But others predicted that the influence is likely to be on the upside.
"The feeling is that the futures boys will try and take the index up before expiry," the salesman said.
Elsewhere domestic economic data included June M4 lending at 0830 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters expected M4 to rise 1.4 percent on the month.
Ahead of the data, sterling continued to hover around the DM3 level.
Traders were also eyeing a German Ifo, or business activity survey at 0800 GMT and an EU monetary committee meeting.
UK gilts opened lower as the negative tone from the U.S. overnight took hold, dealers said.
